text:
Alex: Quick sync — I'm seeing p95 token latency jump ~18% after the int8 kernel rollout + the new continuous-batching heuristic. Profiling attached in comments.
Maria: Where is the regression showing up? GPU or queue wait?
Alex: Mostly queue wait for mid-length requests (30-200 tokens). GPU time per-token down, but batch formation is skewing toward larger batches and causing tail.
Sam: Any KV cache effect? Could be lower hit rate increasing token counts.
Alex: Yeah, KV hit rate dropped ~12% on deploy for the same prompt set. The heuristic currently groups by arrival time + estimated tokens. It doesn't consider KV-hit affinity.
Ira: Can you paste the hot trace?
Alex: Sure — simplified flame: 
```
queue_wait_ms  |  p50: 14   p95: 198  p99: 452
gpu_exec_ms     |  p50: 6    p95: 22   p99: 45
kv_lookup_ms    |  p50: 0.8  p95: 1.2  p99: 3.5
```
Maria: So we have bigger queue waits. That aligns with larger batches forming and waiting for long-stream requests to fill token budget.
Sophia: What's current batch formation policy? Token budget target + max latency cap, right?
Alex: Right — target_token_budget = 1024, max_hold_ms = 80, max_batch_size = 128. Heuristic will wait up to max_hold_ms to hit token budget.
Sam: 1024 feels high for a mixed workload. Long requests hog the budget and reduce KV reuse because of request ordering.
Ira: Proposal: add KV-hit-aware fast-path and a two-tier admission: 
- Fast-path: requests with high kv_hit_prob or short token_est (<32) go to small low-latency batches (budget 128) immediately.
- Bulk-path: everything else participates in normal token_budget batching but with dynamic target scaled by recent p95 queue wait.
Alex: Also add soft budget backpressure: if queue_wait_p95 > 150ms, start returning soft 429s (Retry-After 50ms) for low-priority requests instead of letting them inflate batches.
Maria: I like soft 429 as a signal + immediate fallback to smaller model variant. Could we implement an admission score: score = token_est / target_budget * (1 - kv_hit_prob) + priority_factor ?
Sophia: That seems reasonable. Need to be careful with numeric stability and config explosion. Keep default simple.
Sam: Small experiment idea: two knobs — target_token_budget and kv_affinity_threshold. Run A/B across nodes. Measure p50/p95 queue wait, kv_hit_rate, overall throughput.
Ira: We should also verify kernel selection interactions. Int8 kernels are faster per-token but have different latency variance. When batch size increases, contention for max-seq resources changed. Maybe fallback to fp16 when p95 queue_wait goes up for int8 nodes.
Alex: Good call. Add kernel fallback rule: if int8_node_p95_latency > fp16_node_p95_latency + 10ms for 5m window, route new batches to fp16 variants while throttling int8 nodes for new batch formation.
Maria: For implementation, MVP changes: 
1) Admission: compute kv_hit_prob (from recent per-model rolling window) and token_est from tokenizer.
2) Admission score and two-path dispatch.
3) Soft 429 policy: low-priority requests get soft_reject after soft_reject_ms if queue_wait predicted > threshold.
4) Monitoring: expose new metrics: admit.score_distribution, admit.drop_reason, kv.hit_by_admit_path, kernel.fallback_events.

Config snippet (MVP):
```
admit:
  mode: hybrid
  target_token_budget: 512
  fast_path:
    token_threshold: 32
    kv_hit_prob_threshold: 0.7
    budget: 128
  soft_reject:
    enabled: true
    queue_p95_threshold_ms: 150
    soft_reject_ms: 50
kernel_fallback:
  enabled: true
  window_minutes: 5
  p95_delta_ms: 10
```
Ira: Nice. Experiment plan?
Alex: Roll out on 10% of traffic to a new node pool with these admit knobs. Collect metrics over 6 hours. Key metrics: p50/p95 queue_wait, overall throughput (completed tokens/sec), kv_hit_rate, soft_429_rate, user-level latency.
Sam: Also watch for fairness: don't starve long conversations. Maybe annotate sessions with sticky routing so long-running sessions don't constantly get moved.
Sophia: Could we simulate with the replay infra before rollout? Replay the last 24h and run both policies to estimate impact.
Maria: Yes please, run replay + cost estimate. If p95 improves and throughput ~same or better, we proceed.
Alex: I'll queue a replay job and attach results. Will also add the admit metrics to Grafana dashboards.
build-bot: Replay job 1778201640 queued (replay-2026-03-17). Logs will appear in /replays/1778201640.
Sam: Perfect. If replay looks good, we can ship to 10% and watch kernel_fallback events closely.
Ira: One more thought: for token_budget calculation, use median token length instead of mean to avoid being skewed by tail.
Alex: Agreed. I'll update heuristic to use rolling median and add a fallback percentile config.
Maria: Thanks everyone — let's reconvene after the replay results. :thumbsup:
